title: Deep-Review Eval Case
description: One held-out eval case for the deep-review skill: a PR-context input paired with its expected deep-tier verdict. Each line of evals/deep-review/<split>/cases.jsonl is one object of this shape. Deep review emits a structured verdict — a decision, a risk classification, whether to escalate to the Opus security-audit tier, and grounded key findings — so the expected decision is verdict-shaped (decision / risk / escalate_to_opus / key_findings) — NOT the triage {escalate, risk} shape of evals/case.schema.json. This is the trust anchor for the skill's quality measurement and is CODEOWNER-gated separately from any scorer/proposer.

id.description: Stable, unique kebab-case identifier for the case. Unique within a split and disjoint across dev/holdout (enforced by evals/validate-cases.py).

description.description: Human-readable note on what this case exercises and which shared.md/deep-review.md decision gate grounds the expected verdict.

tags.description: Optional labels for coverage tracking, e.g. the high-risk trigger a case exercises ('auth-secrets', 'db-migration', 'security-anti-pattern', 'unresolved-threads').

input.description: The pre-fetched PR context exactly as deep-review consumes it: title, files changed, diff excerpt, gate signals, and the upstream triage result.

expected.description: The fixed, reward-hack-resistant expected deep-tier verdict the skill must produce for this PR.

decision.description: Whether deep review approves the change or escalates it.

risk.description: Expected risk classification. Any HIGH signal must both escalate and escalate to the Opus security-audit tier.

escalate_to_opus.description: Whether the change must escalate to the Opus security-audit tier. HIGH-risk changes always do; a MEDIUM-risk gate failure escalates on deep review's own findings without the security-audit tier.

key_findings.description: The grounded findings the verdict rests on. At least one, each a non-empty statement tied to a decision gate or high-risk area.
